<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par113 />{{GHGmargin-letter|113|h}}
'''2.''' Analogous to the use of the infinitive absolute as the accusative of the object, mentioned in ''d'', is its employment as a ''casus adverbialis''<ref>That this ''casus adverbialis'' also was originally regarded as an accusative, may be seen from classical Arabic, where an infinitive of this kind expressly retains the accusative ending. In Latin the ablative of the gerund corresponds in many ways to this use of the infinitive absolute.</ref> in connexion with some form of the finite verb, to describe more particularly the manner or attendant circumstances (especially those of time and place) under which an action or state has taken place, or is taking place, or will take place; e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=19}} ''he shall be buried with the burial of an ass'', {{GHGheb|text=סָחוֹב וְהַשְׁלֵךְ|translate=a drawing and casting forth}}, i.e. being drawn and cast forth, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=הַרְחֵק|translate=a removing}}, i.e. distant; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=16}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=30|verse=36}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=6|verse=5}}, 23, 15:35 (where a subject is added subsequently; see below, gg); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=3|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=12}} ({{GHGheb|text=הָחֵל וְכַלֵּה|translate=a beginning and ending}}, i.e. from beginning to end); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=8|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=11}} ({{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֲמֵק}} and {{GHGheb|text=הַגְבֵּהַּ}}, prop. ''a making deep'' ..., and ''a making high'', i.e. whether thy request extend to the world below or to the height above); 57:17 ({{GHGheb|text=הַסְתֵּר|translate=in hiding}}, sc. my face); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=15}} ({{GHGheb|text=דֵּעָה וְהַשְׁכֵּיל|translate=with knowledge and understanding}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=3|verse=13}} ({{GHGheb|text=עָרוֹת}}, for the form cf. {{GHGpar|75|aa}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=חָרֹק}}, to define more precisely {{GHGheb|text=קָֽרְעוּ}} verse 15); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=3}}.<ref>Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=21|verse=13}} for {{GHGheb|text=מָחָה וְהָפַךְ}} read with Stade and Klostermann {{GHGheb|text=מָחֹה וְהָפֹךְ}}; similarly, with Stade, {{GHGheb|text=וְקָשֹׁה}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=24}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְחָזוֹק}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=14}}, and on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=5}} cf. t.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|i}}
Rem. 1. To an adverbial infinitive absolute of this kind, there may further be added a ''casus adverbialis'' (the accusative of state or circumstance), or even a circumstantial clause, to define more exactly the manner in which the action is performed, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=20|verse=2}} ''and he did so'' {{GHGheb|text=הָלֹךְ עָרוֹם וְיָחֵף|translate=walking naked and barefoot}}, prop. in the condition of one naked, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=14}} ''a breaking in pieces'' (acc. to the reading {{GHGheb|text=כָּתוֹת}}; the Masora requires {{GHGheb|text=כָּתוּת}}) ''without sparing''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|k}}
2. A few infinitives of this kind, all of which are in Hiph<sup>e</sup>îl, have, through frequent use, come to be treated by the language as simple adverbs; so especially {{GHGheb|text=הַרְבֵּה}} (cf. {{GHGpar|75|ff}}) ''multum faciendo'', i.e. ''multum'', very frequently strengthened by {{GHGheb|text=מְאֹד|translate=very}} and even used without connexion with a finite verb (see the Lexicon); also {{GHGheb|text=הֵיטֵב|translate=bene faciendo}}, i.e. ''bene'', used especially to express the careful and thorough performance of an action (e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=13|verse=15}}); in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=9|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=27|verse=8|hidebook=1}} it is added epexegetically to another adverbial infinitive absolute, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jon|chapter=4|verse=9}} it twice precedes the verb for the sake of emphasis. Finally, {{GHGheb|text=הַשְׁכֵּם|translate=mane faciendo}}, i.e. ''early in the morning'', then in general ''early'' with the additional idea of earnestness; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=16}} joined with the infinitive absolute {{GHGheb|text=וְהַֽעֲרֵב}} a denominative from {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫רֶב|translate=evening}} (''morning and evening'', i.e. ''early and late)'', elsewhere (with the exception of {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=14}}) always joined with the infinitive absolute of the governing verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=11|verse=7}} ''for I earnestly protested'' ({{GHGheb|text=הַֽעִדֹ֫תִי}}) ''unto your fathers'' ... {{GHGheb|text=הַשֵׁכֵּם וְהָעֵד|translate=rising early and protesting}}, i.e. with earnest protestation; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=26|verse=5|hidebook=1}} (where {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} should be omitted before {{GHGheb|text=ה׳}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=32|verse=33|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=16|verse=15}}.<section end=par113 /><noinclude>
